title: LLM Cache Pricing 2026: The Real Cost of Cached Input
description: LLM cache pricing 2026 normalized across six providers: effective input cost at real hit rates, hidden write fees, and which vendors publish nothing at all.

attribution.citation: Json House, "LLM Cache Pricing 2026: The Real Cost of Cached Input", jsonhouse.com (2026-10-19)

key_facts.fact: Anthropic runs three cache-read multipliers as of 2026-09-28 where it ran one before 2026-09-07: 0.025x base input on Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 (97.5% off), 0.05x on Claude Opus 5.5 and, from 2026-10-14, Claude Sonnet 5.5 (95%), and 0.1x on the rest of its line (90%); DeepSeek reached 98% on deepseek-flash on 2026-09-14; OpenAI left a flat 0.1x on 2026-10-05 with GPT-6.1-sol at 0.05x and Google on 2026-10-14 with Gemini 4 Argon at 0.05x, so none of the three original 0.1x vendors is flat across its line; Mistral sits at a flat 90% and xAI at 75-85%
key_facts.source: Official pricing pages of six providers, retrieved 2026-10-14

key_facts.fact: Effective input price is base x (1 - h) + cache_read x h, where h is the share of input tokens served from cache

The Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite / DeepSeek crossover has moved three times in six weeks — 84.7% before 2026-08-17, 97.6% after that price rise, and 87.7% once deepseek-flash replaced v4-flash on 2026-09-14 — putting it back inside the hit-rate range where long-running agents operate
key_facts.source: jsonhouse calculation from official pricing pages, 2026-08-17

key_facts.fact: OpenAI introduced a 1.25x cache-write charge with the GPT-5.6 family, and GPT-6.1-sol carries it too ($2.50 against a $2.00 base); models before GPT-5.6 had no write fee
key_facts.source: OpenAI prompt caching guide, retrieved 2026-07-28; OpenAI API pricing page, retrieved 2026-10-05

key_facts.fact: GPT-6.1-sol, first observed 2026-10-05, carries GPT-6-sol's $2.00 base input with the cache read halved from $0.20 to $0.10; the two cost the same at a 0% hit rate and GPT-6.1-sol is cheaper at every higher rate, reaching $0.1950 per 1M effective input tokens at 95% against $0.2900 — a reduction a list-price comparison does not show
key_facts.source: jsonhouse calculation from OpenAI API pricing page, retrieved 2026-10-05

key_facts.fact: Anthropic charges 1.25x base input for a 5-minute cache write and 2x for a 1-hour write, has no storage fee, and sets a minimum cacheable prompt length of 512 tokens on Opus 5 and Fable 5 rising to 4,096 on Opus 4.5, Opus 4.6, and Haiku 4.5 — below which requests are processed uncached and without an error
key_facts.source: Anthropic pricing page and prompt caching documentation, retrieved 2026-07-28

key_facts.fact: Google charges no cache write fee but bills storage at $1.00 per 1M cached tokens per hour, rising to $4.50 on Gemini 2.5 Pro and 3.1 Pro Preview

Four of the six providers publish no cache TTL; Mistral's per-model cached-input price, first recorded by this series on 2026-10-14, is 0.1x base input on every model, but Mistral still publishes no cache write price, storage fee or TTL
key_facts.source: jsonhouse normalization of six official documentation sets, 2026-07-28; Mistral API pricing page, retrieved 2026-10-14

key_facts.fact: OpenAI's documentation does not state whether a cache write is billed on a prompt that is never reused; it says an eligible prefix 'may' be cached, and offers prompt_cache_options.mode set to explicit as an opt-out

Eighteen model pairs cross inside the 0-100% hit-rate range on 2026-10-14, up from eleven on 2026-10-05; the lowest is Grok 4.3 x Mistral Medium 3.5 at 83.3%, which enters only because Mistral's cache price was recorded for the first time, followed by Grok 4.6 x Claude Opus 5.5 at 87.0%; six of the seven new pairs come from one $2.00 base / $0.10 cache-read curve now shared by Claude Sonnet 5.5, GPT-6.1-sol and Gemini 4 Argon
key_facts.source: jsonhouse calculation from official pricing pages, 2026-10-14

faq_summary.q: How much does prompt caching actually save in 2026?
faq_summary.a: The discount is 90% on most rows at Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and Mistral, 95% on Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, GPT-6.1-sol and Gemini 4 Argon, 97.5% on Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1, 98% on DeepSeek flash, and 75-85% at xAI. It applies only to the cached share of a prompt, so the realized saving is roughly hit rate times discount — a 50% hit rate against a 90% discount is a 45% cut.

faq_summary.q: Do you pay to write to the cache?
faq_summary.a: Anthropic always charges: 1.25x base input for a 5-minute write, 2x for an hour. OpenAI added the same 1.25x charge with GPT-5.6 and charged nothing before it. Google charges storage per hour instead. xAI, DeepSeek, and Mistral publish no write price.

faq_summary.q: Which LLM API is cheapest for a cache-heavy agent?
faq_summary.a: It depends on the hit rate. Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite is cheapest from 0% through 87.7%, tied there by GPT-6-luna since 2026-09-28 and Claude Haiku 5.5 since 2026-10-14 on identical prices; above that DeepSeek flash wins, reaching $0.0104 per 1M effective input tokens at a 95% hit rate against Flash-Lite's $0.0145. That crossover was 84.7% before 2026-08-17 and 97.6% between then and 2026-09-14.

faq_summary.q: Is prompt caching automatic or do I have to enable it?
faq_summary.a: OpenAI, Google, DeepSeek, and xAI cache automatically; Anthropic requires an explicit cache_control field. Because GPT-5.6 caches automatically above 1,024 tokens and bills writes at 1.25x, a prompt you never reuse may bill above base rate unless you opt out.

faq_summary.q: Why can't I compare cache prices straight from provider pricing pages?
faq_summary.a: No two publish the same fields. Anthropic gives multipliers, DeepSeek an absolute cache-hit price, xAI and Mistral one cached-input column each, and Google a per-hour storage rate on top of a cache-read price. Four of six publish no TTL.

primary_sources.title: xAI prompt caching usage and pricing

comparison_data.unit: USD per 1M input tokens, standard non-batch base tier, collected 2026-10-19 (Monday). No base or cache-read price changed against the 2026-10-14 collection, so every figure below is carried unchanged; DeepSeek replaced the model behind deepseek-flash with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 on 2026-10-17 at the same price. On 2026-10-14 (Wednesday; the 2026-10-12 slot was missed) one existing row changed: Claude Sonnet 5.5's cache read fell from $0.20 to $0.10 and it now has its own entry. Added Gemini 4 Argon and Claude Haiku 5.5; removed Gemini 3.7 Flash (deprecated, routed to Gemini 3.8 Flash). Mistral Medium 3.5 is filled from a cached-input price recorded for the first time, not a changed one. effective_hN = base x (1 - N) + cache_read x N. Gemini 3.6/3.8 Flash are promotional through 2026-12-31 and Gemini 4 Argon through 2026-11-30; Claude Haiku 5.5 figures apply only to prompts up to 100,000 tokens; DeepSeek rows are off-peak and double during weekday peak UTC windows; weekends and Chinese public holidays are off-peak. The DeepSeek flash row replaced the retired v4-flash on 2026-09-14 and is a different model, not a reprice. Effective prices are per token and a token is not a constant amount of text: Claude 4.7 and later count roughly 30% more tokens for the same input than Sonnet 4.6 and earlier, which leaves the discount ratios intact but understates the newer Claude rows in any cross-row price comparison.
